summary: 45 items audited. Coverage of common beans (black, kidney, pinto, cannellini, navy, lima, fava, adzuki, mung, cranberry/borlotti, great northern, flageolet, runner, soy), the cowpea family, chickpeas (desi/kabuli), three lentils (generic + beluga + puy), four South-Asian dals (mung-dal, toor, urad, masoor-as-alias) and a baked-beans flavor cluster is decent. But the taxonomy has real defects: (1) the root 'beans' item carries junk aliases (edamame, faba bean, ful, haricot, bean sprouts) that belong to other items or other categories; (2) there is a true duplicate — 'black-eyed' (black eyed cowpea, child of cowpea) and 'black-eyed-pea' (root) are the same legume; (3) 'cream-cowpea' is mis-tagged with a dairy allergen and stripped of Vegan/Dairy-Free; (4) 'pigeon-pea' and 'toor-dal' both claim the alias 'arhar dal' even though toor IS split pigeon pea — they should be parent/child, not siblings sharing an alias; (5) opaque single-word ids ('barbecue','hickory','maple','original','vegetarian','desi','kabuli','with-skin','dehusked','calico','crowder') are non-self-describing. Gaps that matter for a global, liberal catalog: chana dal (split Bengal gram — the single most-used Indian dal, absent), red/green/brown lentil as named items rather than just facet colors, dried green peas (only fresh peas exist, in Produce), edamame as its own item, plus several regional beans (Lima/butter distinction, black turtle as alias, mottled/Christmas lima, gigante/corona, scarlet runner, French navy/haricot, tepary, moth bean, rice/whole urad, kala chana). Note convention: dried is the catalog default (preservation=dried) for raw pulses; canned items (baked beans, refried, pork-and-beans) correctly default to canned. Fresh green peas/snap/snow live in Produce — keep them there; only DRIED pulses belong here.
issues: Duplicate legume: 'black-eyed' (name 'black eyed cowpea', parent cowpea) and 'black-eyed-pea' (root, aliases black-eyed peas/southern pea) are the same crop (Vigna unguiculata). Two entries with overlapping identity.

Root 'beans' item has misrouted aliases: 'edamame' (should be its own soybean item), 'faba bean' (duplicate of fava), 'ful' (= fava/broad bean, Egyptian ful medames), 'haricot' (= navy bean), 'bean sprout(s)'/'fresh bean sprouts' (a sprouted form, more Produce than dried legume). These pollute the generic root.

'cream-cowpea' has allergens:['dairy'] and dietaryTags missing Vegan and Dairy-Free — cowpeas contain no dairy. Almost certainly a copy/paste bug; should match its cowpea siblings (Vegan, Vegetarian, Gluten-Free, Dairy-Free, Nut-Free).

'pigeon-pea' and 'toor-dal' both list alias 'arhar dal', and toor-dal also aliases 'split pigeon pea'. Toor dal IS split pigeon pea (the dal form of Cajanus cajan). They are modeled as unrelated roots; toor-dal should be a child of pigeon-pea (split form), and 'arhar dal' should not be duplicated across both.

'mung' (whole mung beans) is parented under 'beans', but its split form 'mung-dal' is a separate root with children dehusked/with-skin. Mung dal is the split form of the mung bean — the dal cluster is disconnected from the whole-bean entry, so a user adding 'moong' may land in either tree.

Naming inconsistency in the cowpea tree: child names are 'black eyed cowpea', 'calico cowpea', 'cream cowpea', 'crowder cowpea', 'red cowpea' but several are types whose common names omit 'cowpea' (e.g. crowder peas, cream peas). Acceptable, but 'black eyed cowpea' awkwardly mirrors the separate 'black-eyed pea' root (see duplicate above).

'beluga-lentil' and 'puy' carry facetAliases for colors 'brown' and 'yellow' inherited from generic lentil, but beluga lentils are black and puy lentils are dark green/slate — the color facetAliases are wrong for these specific children.

Opaque ids: 'barbecue','hickory','maple','original','vegetarian' (baked-bean flavors), 'desi','kabuli' (chickpea types), 'calico','crowder' (cowpeas), 'with-skin','dehusked' (mung dal forms) are single generic words with no qualifier in the id. Names disambiguate, but the ids alone are not self-describing and 'vegetarian'/'original' could collide conceptually with other categories.

Generic 'lentil' uses facet colors brown/yellow only; red lentil (masoor, the most common split lentil) and green lentil are not surfaced as named items or distinct facet options — only 'masoor dal' is buried as a lentil alias. Liberal/global catalog should expose red, green, brown lentils explicitly.

Dried green/yellow peas (the whole, dried pulse that becomes split peas) are not represented; only 'split-pea' (legume) and fresh 'pea-green'/'petit-pois'/snap/snow (Produce) exist. Whole dried peas are a distinct pantry pulse.
redundancies: Both are the same crop (Vigna unguiculata, black-eyed pea/cowpea). 'black-eyed' (child of cowpea) and 'black-eyed-pea' (root) duplicate each other. Merge: keep one canonical black-eyed pea, fold 'southern pea'/'black-eyed peas' aliases into it and parent it under cowpea.
Root 'beans' lists alias 'faba bean'; 'fava' is the dedicated fava/broad bean item. The faba-bean alias on the generic root collides with the specific fava item and should move to 'fava'.

'broad' (broad beans) and 'fava' (fava beans) are the same legume (Vicia faba); 'ful' alias on root 'beans' also refers to this. Two distinct items for fava vs broad is a soft redundancy — they are regional names (UK 'broad' = US 'fava'); consider merging or making one an alias-bearing child of the other.
Toor dal is the split/husked dal form of pigeon pea (Cajanus cajan). Modeled as unrelated roots sharing alias 'arhar dal'. Should be parent (pigeon-pea, whole) -> child (toor-dal, split).

'mung' (whole mung bean, child of beans) and 'mung-dal' (split mung, separate root) are the same crop in whole vs split form. The split cluster should hang off the whole bean, not float as an independent root.

newItems.name: chana dal
newItems.notes: Split, husked desi (black) chickpea. The most ubiquitous dal in Indian/South Asian cooking; absent from the catalog entirely. Sister item to ground form 'besan' (gram flour).

newItems.name: kala chana
newItems.notes: Whole small dark desi chickpea, distinct from the larger pale kabuli. Staple across India/Pakistan; chana dal is its split form.

newItems.name: besan
newItems.notes: Flour milled from chana dal; core South-Asian ingredient (pakora, besan chilla, Burmese tofu). Could alternatively live in a flours category, but it is a pulse flour and currently has no home.

newItems.name: red lentil
newItems.notes: Salmon-colored split lentil that cooks fast and breaks down into dal/soup. The single most common lentil worldwide; currently only an alias buried on generic 'lentil'.

newItems.name: green lentil
newItems.notes: Hold-their-shape lentil for salads and side dishes; distinct from beluga (black) and puy (slate). Not surfaced as a named item.

newItems.name: brown lentil
newItems.notes: The default supermarket lentil for stews and soups. Only a facet color today; deserves its own item for recipe matching.

newItems.name: yellow lentil
newItems.notes: Mild quick-cooking yellow lentil used across Mediterranean and South-Asian dals. Currently only a facet color on generic lentil.

newItems.name: edamame
newItems.notes: Immature green soybean, sold fresh/frozen in pod or shelled. Same species as mature soy but a distinct culinary item; currently only a stray alias on root 'beans'. Should default to Frozen storage (not Pantry), unlike dried pulses; contains soy allergen.

newItems.name: dried green peas
newItems.notes: Whole dried Pisum sativum (becomes split pea when decorticated). Distinct from fresh garden peas (in Produce) and from 'split-pea'. Used for mushy peas, pease pudding, dal.

newItems.name: moth bean
newItems.notes: Small brown drought-tolerant Vigna; staple in western India (Maharashtrian misal, sprouted matki). Common pulse with no entry.

newItems.name: gigante beans
newItems.notes: Very large white runner-type bean prized in Greek/Spanish cooking (gigantes plaki). Distinct heirloom size class.

newItems.name: borlotti beans
newItems.notes: OPTIONAL — borlotti is synonymous with cranberry beans (same crop). Prefer adding as aliases on 'cranberry-beans' (see aliasAdditions) rather than a new item; included here only if separate Italian-name shopping is desired. Do not add both.

newItems.name: tepary bean
newItems.notes: Drought-hardy bean native to the US Southwest / northern Mexico (Tohono O'odham heritage food). Niche but globally/culturally notable.

cleanups.fix: Remove allergens:['dairy']; restore dietaryTags to ['Vegan','Vegetarian','Gluten-Free','Dairy-Free','Nut-Free'] to match cowpea siblings. The dairy allergen and missing Vegan/Dairy-Free are a data-entry bug — cowpeas contain no dairy. Also fix gramsPerCup (240 here vs 195 on siblings looks copied from a dairy entry).

Strip misrouted aliases from the generic root: move 'edamame' to a new edamame item, 'faba bean'/'ful' to 'fava', 'haricot' to 'navy'; relocate 'bean sprout(s)'/'fresh bean sprouts' to a sprout item or Produce. Keep only true synonyms of the generic concept ('legume','pulse').
Merge with 'black-eyed-pea' (duplicate crop). Keep a single canonical black-eyed pea, parented under cowpea, carrying aliases black-eyed peas/southern pea/lobia/chawli. Remove the redundant entry.

Set parentIds to ['pigeon-pea'] (toor dal is split pigeon pea) and remove duplicated alias 'arhar dal' from one of the two — keep 'arhar dal' on pigeon-pea (whole) only, or scope it correctly. Currently both float as unrelated roots sharing the alias.
Parent under 'mung' (mung dal is the split form of the mung bean) so whole/split/dehusked/with-skin form one tree, instead of mung-dal being a disconnected root.
Fix inherited color facetAliases: beluga lentils are black, not brown/yellow. Either remove the brown/yellow facetAliases or set a 'black' color option.
Fix inherited color facetAliases: puy lentils are dark green/slate, not brown/yellow. Adjust the color facet to match the actual lentil.
Add the borlotti/romano/rosecoco aliases (see aliasAdditions) so Italian/US/East-African shoppers all resolve to this item; do NOT also create a separate 'borlotti beans' item (would be a duplicate).
dietaryTags correctly omit Vegan/Vegetarian (contains pork) — verify an allergens/meat flag exists if the schema tracks meat; otherwise fine. No change to tags.

Decide canonical model for fava vs broad (same species, Vicia faba): either merge 'broad' into 'fava' with regional aliases, or make 'broad' a child/alias of 'fava'. Currently two sibling items invite double-entry.
